source.name: cheyenne
source.description: OSINT dashboard for satellite imagery acquisition and social media intel geolocation

overview: An earth-observation tracking board for open-source investigators of conflict, humanitarian crises and natural disasters. An interactive globe shows where imaging satellites are right now, what they have already imaged over a place, and what they are scheduled to image next. Free imagery can be drawn on the globe or saved to disk, and live fire detections, ship positions, weather imagery and Telegram reports can be laid over the same map. It runs on your own machine: a small Python server and a browser tab. There is nothing to build, and the core features need no accounts or API keys.

features.title: Live satellite tracking
features.body: Real-time positions, ground tracks and sensor swaths for 23 fleets of imaging satellites: open missions (Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Landsat), daily global sensors (VIIRS, MODIS), commercial optical and radar operators, and state-run systems. The clock can be jumped or accelerated to see where satellites will be.

features.title: Archive search
features.body: For Sentinel-2, Sentinel-1 and Landsat 8/9, footprints of every scene taken over a place in a chosen period, on the globe and on a timeline.

features.title: Future passes
features.body: ESA's published acquisition plans for Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2, and predicted passes for every other fleet, computed from current orbits and sensor geometry.

features.title: Imagery on the globe
features.body: Any open scene can be rendered in place. Only small tiles inside the scene are fetched, so the board stays responsive.

features.title: Visualisations by sensor type
features.body: Optical: true colour, false-colour infrared, shortwave infrared, burn ratio, vegetation, water and moisture indices. Radar: backscatter, dual-polarisation composite, water and flood, strong reflectors. Landsat adds thermal.

features.title: Downloads
features.body: Individual bands as cloud-optimised GeoTIFF, or the current rendering as a PNG.

features.title: Fire detections
features.body: NASA FIRMS near-real-time thermal detections for the last 24 hours, 48 hours or 7 days.

features.title: Ship tracking
features.body: Live AIS positions merged from four free feeds (aisstream.io, Fintraffic, Open Waters and Pelyr), coloured by ship type, with each ship's details and recent track, and a map of where free AIS coverage actually exists.

features.title: Live weather view
features.body: The newest full-disc imagery from the geostationary weather satellites, draped on the globe and refreshed every five minutes.

features.title: Basemaps
features.body: A vector board, or the Esri World Imagery satellite mosaic.

features.title: Intel
features.body: Follows public Telegram channels, places each post on the map with an icon for the kind of event, and raises an alert when a new located report arrives.

features.title: Shareable views
features.body: The address bar records the view, fleet, focus point and time window.

dataSources.source: CelesTrak GP data, cached on disk for 3 hours
Microsoft Planetary Computer (Sentinel-2 L2A, Sentinel-1 GRD, Landsat C2 L2)
ESA Sentinel acquisition plan KML files
NASA FIRMS near-real-time files (VIIRS on NOAA-20/21, MODIS on Terra/Aqua), cached for 20 minutes
GOES-East/West GeoColor via NASA GIBS; Meteosat and geostationary-ring mosaics via EUMETSAT EUMETView

aisstream.io (free key); Fintraffic Digitraffic (CC BY 4.0, no key); Open Waters AIS, including BarentsWatch and the Norwegian Coastal Administration (NLOD 2.0) and AISHub (no key); Pelyr (free key, Pelyr Data Licence 2.0)
GeoNames (CC BY 4.0): every place in 20 countries around the two conflicts, towns over 500 people elsewhere
Anthropic API, claude-haiku-5-5 (optional; needs a login or API key)

footprints.label: PLANNED
footprints.source: ESA acquisition plans for Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2
footprints.reliability: The operator's published schedule. Revised without notice.

footprints.label: PREDICTED (Landsat and other fixed-swath sensors)
footprints.source: Computed from current orbital elements and swath width
footprints.reliability: Good for about a week; Landsat images all daylit land.

footprints.label: PREDICTED (commercial, steerable sensors)
footprints.source: Same computation, using the sensor's pointing range
footprints.reliability: Opportunity only. Whether the operator is tasking the area is not public.

limitations: Predicted passes for commercial satellites show when a satellite could image a place, not whether it will.
Live view. GEOCOLOUR has colour imagery over the Americas, Atlantic, Europe and Africa; Asia and the western Pacific show infrared. The whole-globe mosaics update every 3 hours.
The 7-day FIRMS window downloads about 60 MB on first use and shows the 150,000 strongest detections in view; zoom in to see them all.
Downloads are large. A Sentinel-1 polarisation is roughly 600 MB to 1 GB.
Local use. The server has no user accounts or access control. It binds to 127.0.0.1 by default; do not expose it to the internet.
creditsNote: Cheyenne bundles these third-party components; their licence texts are in web/vendor/licenses/: Data is provided by CelesTrak, ESA and the Copernicus programme, USGS, the Microsoft Planetary Computer, NASA (GIBS and FIRMS), NOAA, EUMETSAT, OpenFreeMap and OpenStreetMap contributors, Esri, GeoNames, aisstream.io, Fintraffic, Open Waters, BarentsWatch and the Norwegian Coastal Administration (Kystverket), and Pelyr. Each provider's own terms apply to its data; the board shows the credits each AIS feed requires while that feed is in use. Cheyenne is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of these providers, or by Telegram or Anthropic.

requirements: Python 3.9 or newer (3.10 or newer for the optional extras)
A current desktop browser with WebGL (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari)
An internet connection, for orbital elements, map tiles and imagery
